A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The comparison includes all eight pages of v1 and all twelve pages of v3, including its three-page supplement. PBC material can be matched across its relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original patch-level and region-level experiments on PBC, ATD, and GenAI in Tables 1–2, alongside qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, baseline comparisons, and training-scale experiments in Tables 1–2 and supplementary Tables A–D.

M1.justification: The proposed ViT/Multiplex Transformer, sampled contrastive loss, edge-aware merging and watershed refinement, and bidirectional region matching remain unchanged. The automatic annotation procedure is also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use PBC and in-house anime-derived training data and evaluate on PBC, ATD, and GenAI. PBC moves into the supplement. The larger training and GenAI evaluation sets change sample counts without establishing a new domain, task, or test scenario.

E2.justification: v1 compares segmentation qualitatively with SAM but provides no quantitative correspondence baseline. v3 adds an adapted Dai et al. (2024) matching framework using TrappedBall segmentation to Table 2 and Figure 6, and adds ClosedRegion and TrappedBall segmentation comparisons while retaining SAM.

E3.justification: The in-house training set increases from 20,000 to 200,000 pairs, while GenAI evaluation increases from 20 to 40 pairs. v3 also introduces experiments at 20k, 100k, and 200k training pairs. ATD and PBC splits, the backbone, batch size, and 20-epoch schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 introduces a controlled training-scale ablation absent from v1. Figure 5 and supplementary Tables A–B evaluate how 20k, 100k, and 200k training pairs affect patch matching and region-level quality, adding substantive evidence about dependence on training-data scale.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: ATD and GenAI results are replaced under revised settings; for example, GenAI cross-image AP changes from 84.48% to 83.49%. New baseline and scaling results are added: v3 Table 2 reports region accuracy of 84.44% versus 82.94% on ATD and 78.43% versus 72.36% on GenAI. PBC numerical results are retained except that its 21.37% region recall, like the other exact region-recall entries, is omitted.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and their underlying definitions and reasoning are retained. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and v3 does not provide a new mathematical definition for its 'Region Accuracy' label.

C1.justification: The task novelty, proposed framework, and annotation contributions remain the same. The abstract shifts its headline evidence from a 96.34% patch-level score to 78.4–84.4% region-level accuracy and adds an explicit claim that training suppresses noisy matches and strengthens consistent structural relationships.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for ClosedRegion failure and TrappedBall over-segmentation, attributes ATD's higher top-K accuracy to training-domain alignment, and interprets scaling gains as better structural representations. It also expands the PBC granularity–recall discussion. The existing limitation concerning small regions and lost facial details is retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents how to construct and decode the adapted pseudo-coloring baseline and discloses a CR target of 1.4–1.7 for post-processing selection. Its hardware description changes from a single A100 to unspecified A100 GPUs. Core implementation settings and the promise to release annotation tools and evaluation data remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zhang et al.'s 'Vectorizing cartoon animations' reference for TrappedBall and positions the already-cited Dai et al. framework as an adapted empirical comparator. The broader literature coverage and first-task novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is substantially rewritten, introduction and related-work prose are revised, and the narrative explicitly prioritizes realistic manga-style inputs. Experiments gain a dedicated baseline subsection, PBC material is reorganized into Supplement B, and the separate limitations discussion is incorporated into qualitative results and the conclusion.

P2.justification: v3 restructures benchmark tables to include baseline rows and replaces separate region precision/recall columns with 'Region Accuracy.' It replaces the cross-dataset PR plot with training-scale curves, adds ablation tables, rebuilds the GenAI qualitative comparison, and relocates PBC tables and illustrations into the supplement. The principal method diagrams remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The quantitative correspondence baseline and training-scale ablation add useful validation missing from v1. The net gain is limited by weaker reporting clarity: exact region recall disappears, 'Region Accuracy' is not reconciled with precision/recall terminology, and the 200k GenAI results differ without clear explanation between the main and supplementary tables, including 78.43% versus 70.44% region accuracy. The additional comparisons strengthen the paper modestly, but these gaps limit confidence in its stronger performance presentation.
